title: Date Palm: Ancient Date Palms You Can Visit
meta_description: A desert palm grown tall in European gardens. Valencia's La Carcasa grows more than 35 trunks from one base, like a firework mid-burst.
intro: A date palm belongs to an oasis, not a city square, yet a handful have made themselves at home in European parks and gardens. Lisbon's, in the Ninth of April Garden, is the most argued over: the city calls it the tallest tree in the capital at 38 metres, the national register measured it at 26.7, and nobody has climbed up to settle it. Palermo's stands over a Roman mosaic of Alexander the Great hunting a lion, unearthed by accident under Villa Bonanno and left where it was found. A date palm is meant to grow as a single trunk, and two of these refuse. Seville's forks into a cluster in the Parque de Maria Luisa. Valencia's La Carcasa, in the university's botanic garden, grows more than 35 trunks from one base and is named for the spent casing of a firework shell.
